rules.reason: Do not create folders at the root of a drive. Put it under D:\tmp instead - that directory exists and is the place for scratch, demo and test output that does not belong in the project tree (build.claude/ or similar). This applies to a script's default output path too: running the script is the same act as writing the files directly, so change the default rather than passing an override. The path '{name}' does not exist, so this would create it.

Plain Claude subagents are off here (ATRIUM_ONLY_SUBAGENTS). Run substantive agent work as a REAL atrium session instead, so it is watchable on the board and kept in history. HARD RULE, check FIRST: call the atrium-control MCP tool atrium_peers and count the running sessions YOU launched (sessions the user started do not count); if you launched 10 or more (the concurrency cap), do NOT launch another -- wait for one to finish or ask clint, do not spawn past the cap. Otherwise: (1) make/prepare the working directory first -- it must already exist; (2) call atrium_launch with cwd, a short title, a one-line why, and a FULL prompt containing the ENTIRE task (the new session inherits NONE of this conversation's context, so spell it all out); (3) use the returned card id with atrium_task / atrium_say to follow up. If a normal one-shot subagent is genuinely wanted this session, the user can set ATRIUM_ONLY_SUBAGENTS=0 and retry.
Never add a Co-Authored-By trailer to a commit message or PR description, and never suggest one. No attribution or co-author line of any kind, ever. This is absolute.
go build must write to build.claude. Add -o build.claude/ (directory form works for ./... too).
claude may not create or unset git aliases (an alias can hide a blocked verb or run a shell command). Hand it to the user.
'git {name}' sets git configuration for one command, and configuration can run a program (core.pager, core.sshCommand, http.extraHeader...). Run the git command without it, or hand it to the user.
git alias '{name}' is a shell alias ('!...') or a chain of aliases that does not end -- claude may not run it. Run the real git verb instead, or hand it to the user.

'git {name}' is not a git command, or is an alias claude cannot resolve here, or an external git program, or a git lfs verb that reaches a remote. Any of those could reach a remote unseen, so it is blocked. Use the real git verb, or hand it to the user.

claude never pushes, pulls, or fetches -- no git command may reach a remote. Hand it to the user. The one exception is atrium's hub remote: exactly 'git push hub <branch>', 'git push -u hub <branch>' or 'git fetch hub', optionally after one 'cd <dir>' (newline or &&), and only when that remote points at this room's atrium forwarder.
Use 'git switch claude/<branch>' to move branches. Plain 'git checkout' is blocked here (ambiguous with file restore, and claude stays on claude/* branches).
claude may only create, switch to, delete or rename claude/* branches. '{name}' is not one.
claude may only run that git verb on a claude/* branch ({name}). Switch to a claude/* branch, or hand the command to the user.
Do not use compound 'cd /path && command' patterns. Run 'cd /path' as a standalone command first, then run subsequent commands without cd prefixes.
Do not use 'find' in bash. Use glob patterns instead.
Do not use perl. Use bash (or the dedicated file/search/edit tools) instead.

Do not use python unless bash or PowerShell genuinely cannot solve the problem. Prefer bash, pwsh, or the dedicated file/search/edit tools. If python is actually required for this, say why and ask the user first.
Do not prefix inline env vars before docker (e.g. 'FOO=bar docker ...'). Pass env explicitly: 'docker run -e VAR=val', a compose block, or '--env-file'.
Do not chain multiple commands with ';'. Run one command at a time.
Use tee instead of > or >> for output redirection.

This repo uses CMake presets -- run cmake THROUGH the preset so its environment (VCPKG_BINARY_SOURCES, the shared vcpkg installed dir) applies. A bare cmake reconfigures with the shell env, misses the vcpkg binary cache, and rebuilds every port from source. Configure: cmake --preset <name> (e.g. cwdming). Build: cmake --build --preset <name> (or cmake --build <preset-build-dir> only if you are certain no reconfigure will trigger).
gh api .../pulls/<n>/comments is the correct endpoint for inline review comments.
gh api calls must start with: gh api -X GET
Do not modify CMake presets, vcpkg.json, triplet files, or overlay ports without asking first. These can trigger expensive vcpkg rebuilds. Ask the user before editing.
Never use the em-dash character (U+2014). Rewrite the sentence: split it, or use a comma, parentheses, or a colon.
Never add !important to CSS rules. Rework the selector specificity instead.
default.env is a non-secret template, so writing it is allowed.
Do not write .env files (they hold secrets). Only default.env may be written.
